meta.about: Minda Corporation Ltd is one of the leading automotive component manufacturing companies in India with a pan-India presence and international footprint. It is the flagship company of Spark Minda, which was part of the erstwhile Minda Group.[1] The company was formed after a split between the businesses of the Minda brothers in 2012. Presently, NK Minda owns and operates Minda Industries Ltd and Ashok Minda is the owner of Minda Corporation Ltd. [2] Both the companies are listed on the exchanges.
meta.keyPoints: Business Segments 1. Electrical Distribution Systems (Wiring Harness & Connectors)[1][2] This segment focuses on low- and high-voltage wiring harnesses, smart junction boxes, and EV high-voltage connection systems. It's key products include EV HV wiring harnesses (with a strategic order from a leading PV OEM), connectors, busbars, CCS wires, and EV PDUs/BDUs, supported by localization via a SANCO China tie-up.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Minda Corporation Ltd (consolidated, Rs crore). FY26 is the last reported year (revenue Rs6,185 cr). One reported segment; revenue is a single growth path computed from the vertical build in `build` (Mechatronics organic, Information & Connected Systems, Minda Vast consolidated from FY27) and checked in tools/authoring/MINDACORP.ctx.js. Net profit is on the owners' basis and per-share figures on 24.673 cr fully diluted shares (MINDACORP.patch.js: promoter warrants treated as converted, Rs315.56 cr balance added to cash). The engine has no line for the share of associate/JV profit (post-tax, mainly 49% of Flash Electronics) or minorities, so both enter `otherIncome` grossed up for tax (see _otherIncomeWhy). Forecasts exclude the Q1FY27 Rs106 cr one-off gain on consolidating Minda Vast. Valued on P/E, as the street does; the multiple is derived in MINDACORP.ctx.js and written here by MINDACORP.val.js.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the vertical build. FY27E +24.8%: Q1FY27 +33% reported, ~+24% organic (Minda Vast added ~Rs125 cr); Vast adds ~Rs560 cr for the year (FY26 ~Rs500 cr, Q1 +22%). Organic: Mechatronics +12% (Q1 ex-Vast +14%), ICS +19% (Q1 +34%: harness >30%, clusters >35%), slowing from Q3 against the GST-boosted base; Q2-Q4 organic growth implied ~14%. FY28E +14.2% and FY29E +14.1%: production +5-7% plus content (TFT clusters, HV harness, smart access), switch JV (Toyodenso, SOP Q4FY27; ~Rs150 cr in FY28, peak FY29) and die-casting exports; sunroof (HCMF) and Turntide are equity-accounted JVs, not revenue. Management's 'at least 1.5x industry' and Vision 2030 need ~19-20%; street FY27E/FY28E/FY29E revenue Rs7,362-7,653 / 8,679-8,830 / 9,909-10,260 cr.
assumptions._marginWhy: FY26 11.7%; Q1FY27 11.5% (11.9% in Q4FY26) with Vast at 8.4% diluting ~25bp. CFO: 11.5-12% for the rest of FY27 with back-to-back commodity pass-through (1-2 quarter lag); 12.5% by FY30 (Vision 2030). We assume 11.6% / 11.8% / 12.0% as Vast's margin improves and operating leverage offsets wage and commodity inflation. Range since FY21: 9.2-11.7%. Street: Emkay 11.7/11.9/11.9%, MNCL 11.6/12.0/12.2%, Choice 11.6/11.9/12.0%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 Rs413 cr (record). FY27 guided ~Rs400-450 cr (22-May-2026) and ~Rs400 cr (13-Aug-2026); Vast's capex is now consolidated, so Rs450 cr. Vision 2030: ~Rs2,000 cr over five years (two die-casting greenfields, one cluster plant, land bought in FY26). Emkay Rs454/450/400 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs230 cr = 9.0% of average gross block (Rs2,566 cr); Q1FY27 Rs69 cr (incl. Minda Vast, consolidated from Apr-2026) runs at ~Rs280 cr a year. Vast's fixed assets are not in the FY26 base (gap), so 9.5%: FY27E ~Rs278 cr, FY28E ~Rs320 cr, FY29E ~Rs363 cr (Emkay Rs277 / 311 / 358 cr). The engine depreciates new capex at once and keeps CWIP flat.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt company (Rs1,065 cr at Mar-2026 excl. leases; Rs750 cr pro forma for the warrant balance). The engine's 'treasury' nets the Flash (Rs1,474 cr) and JV stakes held at book in investments against debt, so it is positive; that is not cash and earns no interest. Interest income is small and sits in recurring other income.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged: (1) recurring other income Rs12 / 14 / 16 cr (FY26 Rs15 cr, Q1FY27 Rs2 cr); (2) share of associate and JV profit, post-tax, Rs77 / 100 / 125 cr: Flash 49% Rs80 / 100 / 122 cr (FY26 ~Rs70 cr; Flash guides 20-24% growth and a 16-17% margin; Q1FY27 ~Rs18 cr after PPA depreciation) plus Furukawa (17.5%) ~Rs5-8 cr, less start-up losses at HCMF (sunroof), Turntide and Infac; Vast leaves this line (FY26 Rs5 cr) as it is consolidated; Emkay Rs77 / 104 / 133 cr; less (3) minorities Rs6 / 12 / 16 cr (50% of Vast's profit; 40% of the Toyodenso JV once profitable). (2) and (3) are after tax, so they are divided by (1 - 27%) because the engine taxes all other income: 12 + (77 - 6) / 0.73 = Rs109 cr. Net profit then equals owners' PAT. FY26 on the engine's basis: other income Rs14 cr (Screener) plus associates Rs81 cr below the tax line.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs122 cr (Flash acquisition debt for a full year), Q1FY27 Rs31 cr. Gross debt Rs1,212 cr plus leases Rs259 cr at Mar-2026; the Rs316 cr warrant balance (due by Dec-2026) and free cash flow cut debt from H2FY27 (Emkay net debt Rs1,324 cr FY26 to Rs826 cr FY28E).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on profit before associates: FY26 27.7%, FY25 28.6%, Q1FY27 27.4% excluding the gain on Vast (20.7% reported). New-regime rate 25.2% plus disallowances and loss-making start-ups.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Rs1.40 a share for FY26 = 9% of EPS; 9-15% since FY22.

build._note: Vertical build (Rs crore). FY26 base from the Q4FY26 presentation (Mechatronics, Aftermarket & Others Rs2,843 cr; ICS Rs3,342 cr; total = reported Rs6,185 cr). Minda Vast (50%, consolidated from 1-Apr-2026) is a separate line. Checked against model revenue in MINDACORP.ctx.js.
build._why: Mechatronics (vehicle access, die casting, aftermarket, EV systems): Q1 ex-Vast +14%; die-casting export plant (Pune), switch JV from Q4FY27 (Rs650 cr target by 2030), aftermarket steady. ICS: Q1 +34%; TFT cluster orders entering SOP across PV/CV/2W, HV harness and connector localisation; harness share gains in 2W/3W/CV (Japanese PV makers are served by Furukawa Minda, an associate). Vast: FY26 ~Rs500 cr, Q1 +22%; +15% a year as smart-access content grows.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical auto supplier with moderate leverage (net debt ~0.3x equity pro forma): beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%. Debt is ~5% of enterprise value, so we use the cost of equity as the discount rate (the engine's DCF has no separate WACC in Excel).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; vehicle production ~5-6% plus content. House range 5-6%: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~14% to 8% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 12.0%: above the 9-12% history, below the 12.5% Vision 2030 target.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~4.5% of revenue in FY29E to 4.0% (FY22-26 average ~7%); depreciation 3.5% of revenue (FY26 3.7%).
dcf._assocWhy: FCFF excludes associate profit (mainly Flash); Flash and the JVs enter only at book value (Rs1,474 cr and ~Rs90 cr) through investments in the engine's net cash. The DCF therefore understates Flash's value (see the DCF chapter).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Volumes keep growing high single digits after the GST step; TFT clusters, HV harness, smart access and the switch JV ramp on time; Vast's margin converges to the group's; commodity costs ease; margin moves towards the 12.5% Vision 2030 target.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Volumes flatten against the GST base; commodity and wage inflation is recovered late; 2W EV makers in-source electronics; Flash's margin stays near 15%; new JVs lose money for longer; margin slips back to ~11%.

cover.headline: Good growth, a costly EV bet and a full price: the multiple, not the business, sets the call
cover.lead: Minda Corporation (Spark Minda) makes wiring harnesses, instrument clusters, vehicle-access systems and die castings, mainly for two-wheelers and trucks, and owns 49% of Flash Electronics (EV and two-wheeler power electronics). Revenue grew 21% a year over FY21-26 and the EBITDA margin rose to 11.7%; Q1FY27 revenue rose 33% (~24% organic, the rest from consolidating Minda Vast). We forecast EPS of ₹18.0 / ₹22.3 / ₹27.3 for FY27-29E on the fully diluted share count (promoter warrants at ₹550 treated as converted), 6-8% below the street (3-5% before the dilution). The street values Minda Corp on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (32-34x FY28E/Jun-28E). The house rule (its own forward P/E median since 2021 on EPS before one-offs, 28.4x, cut by the 8.8% auto-component de-rating) gives **26x Sep-28E EPS of ₹24.8 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹635, DCF ₹477. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core business is growing well
arguments.p: Wiring harnesses (31% of FY26 revenue) and instrument clusters (17%) grew 30-35% in Q1FY27 on premiumisation (TFT clusters, high-voltage harnesses) and share gains in two-wheelers and trucks; the Information & Connected Systems vertical grew 29% in FY26. Lifetime orders of ₹10,000 cr in FY26 and ₹2,500 cr in Q1FY27. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct0}} (FY27E includes ~₹560 cr from Minda Vast).

arguments.h: Flash is the EV story, and it is expensive
arguments.p: Minda paid ₹1,372 cr for 49% of Flash (Jan-2025). Flash grew 17% in FY26 to ₹1,803 cr at a 17.2% EBITDA margin and 42% in Q1FY27, but its profit reaches Minda only as a share of profit (₹70 cr in FY26, ~5% on the price paid) and its Q1 margin fell to 15.4%. We expect ₹77 / 100 / 125 cr of associate profit, 18% of FY28E profit.

arguments.h: Margins are rising, but they are tier-1 margins
arguments.p: EBITDA margin rose from 9.3% (FY21) to 11.7% (FY26); Q1FY27 was 11.5% with Minda Vast (8.4%) diluting. Management guides 11.5-12% for FY27 and 12.5% by FY30. Commodity costs are passed through with a 1-2 quarter lag and no mark-up, so there is no pricing power to push margins much higher. ROE is 14-16% in our forecasts.

At ₹693 the stock trades at 31.0x our FY28E and 27.9x Sep-28E EPS, against its own forward median of 28.4x since 2021; auto-component stocks sat 8.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. The street's 32-34x on undiluted EPS ~5% above ours is what gets it to ₹815-867. We like the direction of the business; the price already pays for it.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter against the GST-boosted base from Q3, Minda Vast margin, Flash margin recovery from 15.4%.
Conversion of the promoter's 76.5 lakh warrants (₹316 cr balance due within 18 months of the Jun-2025 allotment, i.e. by Dec-2026): 3.2% dilution, debt reduction.
Start of production: sunroofs (HCMF JV, Q2FY27), Turntide motor controllers (guided Oct-Nov 2026), Toyodenso switches (Q4FY27).
Festive-season production (Oct-Dec 2026) in two-wheelers and trucks, Minda Corp's two largest end markets.
New orders and Vision 2030 progress: exports (₹420 cr in FY25, target ₹1,500 cr by FY30), PV share (19% in Q1FY27, target 25%).

sections.title: Wiring, clusters, locks and castings for two-wheelers and trucks, plus 49% of an EV electronics maker

blocks.p: Minda Corporation is the listed flagship of the Spark Minda group, controlled by Ashok Minda's family (64.8%). It is a different company from Uno Minda: the two Minda brothers split the group in 2012. It makes wiring harnesses and connectors, instrument clusters, vehicle-access and security systems (ignition locks, handles, immobilisers, smart keys), aluminium die castings, interior plastics and EV electronics in 42 plants, and sells spares under the Spark Minda brand. In FY26, two- and three-wheelers were 48% of revenue, commercial vehicles and tractors 28%, passenger vehicles 14% and the aftermarket 10%; 89% was billed in India. It reports one segment but discloses revenue for two verticals. Around it sit equity-accounted associates and JVs: Flash Electronics (49%), Furukawa Minda (17.5%, harnesses for Japanese car makers), and new JVs with HCMF (sunroofs), Turntide (EV motors) and, consolidated, Toyodenso (switches). Including Flash, Vast and Furukawa, "group" revenue was ~₹9,016 cr in FY26.

sections.title: From restructuring to deal-making: KTSN write-off, Pricol exit, Flash purchase, Vast control

blocks.p: After the 2012 family split, Minda Corp spent the rest of the decade cleaning up: the German plastics unit Minda KTSN went insolvent and was written off, and the write-off was later allowed as a tax deduction, which is why FY23 tax was ~1% (Screener also shows ₹196 cr and ₹41 cr of exceptional losses after tax in FY20-21). It built a 15.7% stake in rival Pricol (cost ~₹400 cr) amid talk of a combination that the competition regulator questioned, and sold it in Jan-2024 for ₹658 cr. The proceeds and new debt went into 49% of Flash Electronics in Jan-2025. In FY26 it signed three technology JVs, and from Apr-2026 it consolidates Minda Vast after changing the shareholders' agreement with VAST. Each step changed what "earnings" means, which matters for the valuation history.

sections.title: Record vehicle production in Q1FY27 (+22%) after GST cuts; commodity costs are the catch

blocks.p: India produced ~34.7 mn vehicles in FY26 (+12%), with a strong second half after the Sep-2025 GST cuts. bullets: **The tailwind reaches it.** FY26 growth was nearly twice production growth, helped by harness and cluster premiumisation; management attributes 12-13 points of Q4FY26's 29% growth to premiumisation and new products.
**But it is cyclical.** In FY24-25, when trucks and exports slowed, revenue grew only 8-9% a year. Q1FY27 organic growth (~24%) was only a little above production (+22%).

blocks.p: Wiring harnesses (31% of FY26 revenue) and instrument clusters (17%) are the growth engine. Japanese car makers are served by Furukawa Minda, an associate, so Minda Corp's own harness business is mostly 2W/3W/CV. Clusters are moving from analogue to TFT screens (3-15 inch) across two-wheelers, trucks and cars, with platform-level orders from several OEMs entering production in FY27. sections.title: Flash Electronics: a good EV business bought at a full price; associates ~18% of FY28E profit

blocks.p: Flash Electronics makes magnetos, alternators, regulator-rectifiers, motors, motor controllers and chargers for two- and three-wheelers, with plants in India, Germany and Hungary and customers including Bajaj, Royal Enfield, Suzuki, Yamaha, Piaggio and Mahindra as well as KTM, Ducati, Triumph, BMW, Audi and Porsche. blocks.callout: **Verdict: no durable moat, a decent franchise.** Minda Corp is an established, mid-sized supplier to most Indian two-wheeler and truck makers, moving up the value chain in harnesses and clusters with partners' help. Its listed rivals (Motherson Sumi Wiring in harnesses, Pricol in instrument clusters) are larger or as capable in their niches, margins have never exceeded 12%, and commodity costs are passed through without a margin. Growth and returns depend on winning programmes one by one.

sections.title: Revenue up 2.6x since the Covid year, margin up from 9% to 12%: a quiet re-build

blocks.p: Minda Corp's revenue was ₹2,435 cr in FY16 and barely higher, ₹2,368 cr, in FY21: five lost years of restructuring (a German plastics subsidiary, KTSN, went insolvent and was written off) and two weak vehicle years. Since then it has grown 21% a year to ₹6,185 cr in FY26, well ahead of vehicle production (FY26: +22% vs ~+12%). The EBITDA margin rose every year, from 9.3% (FY21) to 11.7% (FY26), as wiring harnesses and instrument clusters moved up the value chain (TFT clusters, high-voltage harnesses, in-house connectors). Owners' EPS went from ₹2.2 (FY21) to ₹15.1 (FY26), but FY22-23 were flattered by one-offs (exceptional gains and a one-time tax benefit): on the company's normalised profit, EPS rose from ₹5.7 (FY22) to ₹15.1, 27% a year. From FY26 a growing part of profit is the 49% share of Flash Electronics (₹70 cr), which sits below EBITDA.

sections.title: Capital allocation: one big bet (Flash, ₹1,372 cr), partly paid for by selling Pricol

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Minda Corp generated ₹2,147 cr of operating cash and spent ₹1,490 cr on capex, so the core business funds itself. The big moves were financial. In Jan-2024 it sold its 15.7% stake in Pricol for ₹658 cr (bought for ~₹400 cr during a contested stake-building; the gain went through other comprehensive income, not profit). A year later it paid ₹1,372 cr for 49% of Flash Electronics (EV and two-wheeler power electronics, motors), funded largely with debt: gross debt went from ₹348 cr (Mar-24) to ₹1,344 cr (Mar-25). The promoter then took 76.5 lakh warrants at ₹550 (₹421 cr; 25% paid in Jun-2025, the rest due by Dec-2026). Capex is guided at ~₹400-450 cr for FY27 and ~₹2,000 cr over five years (Vision 2030).

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit and good cash conversion, but one-offs in three of the last five years

bullets: **Cash conversion is good.** Cash from operations was ₹676 cr in FY26, 188% of owners' profit and 94% of EBITDA; operating cash has exceeded capex every year since FY22.

**One-offs are frequent.** FY22 and FY23 profit included exceptional gains and a one-time tax benefit (normalised PAT ₹137 cr and ₹219 cr vs ₹192 cr and ₹284 cr reported); FY20-21 had large exceptional losses; Q1FY27 has a ₹106 cr (after tax) fair-value gain on Minda Vast. We use the company's normalised profit in the valuation history and forecast no one-offs.

**Associate profit is a growing share of EPS.** ₹81 cr in FY26 (22% of profit), rising to ~₹100 cr by FY28E. It is after Flash's acquisition-related depreciation (not disclosed separately), and the cash reaches Minda only as dividends.
**The Pricol gain bypassed profit.** The ₹239 cr gain on the Pricol sale went through other comprehensive income (Ind AS 109), so it never inflated EPS; it did fund the Flash purchase.

**Audit trail.** The auditor (S R Batliboi, EY) notes that some accounting software at the company and at several JVs/associates did not keep a complete audit trail: a process weakness, not a misstatement.
**Vast changes the comparisons.** From FY27 revenue, EBITDA and minorities include Minda Vast; the associate line loses it. Year-on-year growth in FY27 is flattered by ~9 points.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unqualified audit and solid cash conversion. The amber is for the run of one-offs (gains, a tax benefit, a fair-value gain), the growing associate line whose amortisation is not disclosed, and the audit-trail exceptions.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than five years ago, priced at 27.9x Sep-28E EPS; SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a promoter-run Indian auto-parts maker that has re-built itself since FY21 (revenue 2.6x, margin 9% to 12%), with a strong position in two-wheeler and truck wiring harnesses, clusters and locks, a 49% stake in a fast-growing EV electronics maker (Flash), and new JVs in switches, sunroofs and EV motors. Revenue should grow ~15% a year after FY27 and EPS ~23% a year to FY29E. Margins are tier-1 margins (~12%) and returns on equity are middling (14-16%) because of the price paid for Flash.

**What you are paying:** 38.4x our FY27E and 31.0x FY28E EPS (fully diluted). Since 2021 the market has paid a median 28.4x forward for Minda Corp, and auto-component stocks were 8.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. On the street's own method and the house multiple the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): SELL. assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Minda Corporation Ltd (consolidated, Rs crore). FY26 is the last reported year (revenue Rs6,185 cr). One reported segment; revenue is a single growth path computed from the vertical build in `build` (Mechatronics organic, Information & Connected Systems, Minda Vast consolidated from FY27) and checked in tools/authoring/MINDACORP.ctx.js. Net profit is on the owners' basis and per-share figures on 24.673 cr fully diluted shares (MINDACORP.patch.js: promoter warrants treated as converted, Rs315.56 cr balance added to cash). The engine has no line for the share of associate/JV profit (post-tax, mainly 49% of Flash Electronics) or minorities, so both enter `otherIncome` grossed up for tax (see _otherIncomeWhy). Forecasts exclude the Q1FY27 Rs106 cr one-off gain on consolidating Minda Vast. Valued on P/E, as the street does; the multiple is derived in MINDACORP.ctx.js and written here by MINDACORP.val.js.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the vertical build. FY27E +24.8%: Q1FY27 +33% reported, ~+24% organic (Minda Vast added ~Rs125 cr); Vast adds ~Rs560 cr for the year (FY26 ~Rs500 cr, Q1 +22%). Organic: Mechatronics +12% (Q1 ex-Vast +14%), ICS +19% (Q1 +34%: harness >30%, clusters >35%), slowing from Q3 against the GST-boosted base; Q2-Q4 organic growth implied ~14%. FY28E +14.2% and FY29E +14.1%: production +5-7% plus content (TFT clusters, HV harness, smart access), switch JV (Toyodenso, SOP Q4FY27; ~Rs150 cr in FY28, peak FY29) and die-casting exports; sunroof (HCMF) and Turntide are equity-accounted JVs, not revenue. Management's 'at least 1.5x industry' and Vision 2030 need ~19-20%; street FY27E/FY28E/FY29E revenue Rs7,362-7,653 / 8,679-8,830 / 9,909-10,260 cr.
assumptions._marginWhy: FY26 11.7%; Q1FY27 11.5% (11.9% in Q4FY26) with Vast at 8.4% diluting ~25bp. CFO: 11.5-12% for the rest of FY27 with back-to-back commodity pass-through (1-2 quarter lag); 12.5% by FY30 (Vision 2030). We assume 11.6% / 11.8% / 12.0% as Vast's margin improves and operating leverage offsets wage and commodity inflation. Range since FY21: 9.2-11.7%. Street: Emkay 11.7/11.9/11.9%, MNCL 11.6/12.0/12.2%, Choice 11.6/11.9/12.0%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 Rs413 cr (record). FY27 guided ~Rs400-450 cr (22-May-2026) and ~Rs400 cr (13-Aug-2026); Vast's capex is now consolidated, so Rs450 cr. Vision 2030: ~Rs2,000 cr over five years (two die-casting greenfields, one cluster plant, land bought in FY26). Emkay Rs454/450/400 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs230 cr = 9.0% of average gross block (Rs2,566 cr); Q1FY27 Rs69 cr (incl. Minda Vast, consolidated from Apr-2026) runs at ~Rs280 cr a year. Vast's fixed assets are not in the FY26 base (gap), so 9.5%: FY27E ~Rs278 cr, FY28E ~Rs320 cr, FY29E ~Rs363 cr (Emkay Rs277 / 311 / 358 cr). The engine depreciates new capex at once and keeps CWIP flat.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt company (Rs1,065 cr at Mar-2026 excl. leases; Rs750 cr pro forma for the warrant balance). The engine's 'treasury' nets the Flash (Rs1,474 cr) and JV stakes held at book in investments against debt, so it is positive; that is not cash and earns no interest. Interest income is small and sits in recurring other income.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged: (1) recurring other income Rs12 / 14 / 16 cr (FY26 Rs15 cr, Q1FY27 Rs2 cr); (2) share of associate and JV profit, post-tax, Rs77 / 100 / 125 cr: Flash 49% Rs80 / 100 / 122 cr (FY26 ~Rs70 cr; Flash guides 20-24% growth and a 16-17% margin; Q1FY27 ~Rs18 cr after PPA depreciation) plus Furukawa (17.5%) ~Rs5-8 cr, less start-up losses at HCMF (sunroof), Turntide and Infac; Vast leaves this line (FY26 Rs5 cr) as it is consolidated; Emkay Rs77 / 104 / 133 cr; less (3) minorities Rs6 / 12 / 16 cr (50% of Vast's profit; 40% of the Toyodenso JV once profitable). (2) and (3) are after tax, so they are divided by (1 - 27%) because the engine taxes all other income: 12 + (77 - 6) / 0.73 = Rs109 cr. Net profit then equals owners' PAT. FY26 on the engine's basis: other income Rs14 cr (Screener) plus associates Rs81 cr below the tax line.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs122 cr (Flash acquisition debt for a full year), Q1FY27 Rs31 cr. Gross debt Rs1,212 cr plus leases Rs259 cr at Mar-2026; the Rs316 cr warrant balance (due by Dec-2026) and free cash flow cut debt from H2FY27 (Emkay net debt Rs1,324 cr FY26 to Rs826 cr FY28E).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on profit before associates: FY26 27.7%, FY25 28.6%, Q1FY27 27.4% excluding the gain on Vast (20.7% reported). New-regime rate 25.2% plus disallowances and loss-making start-ups.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Rs1.40 a share for FY26 = 9% of EPS; 9-15% since FY22.

build._note: Vertical build (Rs crore). FY26 base from the Q4FY26 presentation (Mechatronics, Aftermarket & Others Rs2,843 cr; ICS Rs3,342 cr; total = reported Rs6,185 cr). Minda Vast (50%, consolidated from 1-Apr-2026) is a separate line. Checked against model revenue in MINDACORP.ctx.js.
build._why: Mechatronics (vehicle access, die casting, aftermarket, EV systems): Q1 ex-Vast +14%; die-casting export plant (Pune), switch JV from Q4FY27 (Rs650 cr target by 2030), aftermarket steady. ICS: Q1 +34%; TFT cluster orders entering SOP across PV/CV/2W, HV harness and connector localisation; harness share gains in 2W/3W/CV (Japanese PV makers are served by Furukawa Minda, an associate). Vast: FY26 ~Rs500 cr, Q1 +22%; +15% a year as smart-access content grows.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical auto supplier with moderate leverage (net debt ~0.3x equity pro forma): beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%. Debt is ~5% of enterprise value, so we use the cost of equity as the discount rate (the engine's DCF has no separate WACC in Excel).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; vehicle production ~5-6% plus content. House range 5-6%: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~14% to 8% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 12.0%: above the 9-12% history, below the 12.5% Vision 2030 target.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~4.5% of revenue in FY29E to 4.0% (FY22-26 average ~7%); depreciation 3.5% of revenue (FY26 3.7%).
